title: The Séance
logline: Seven years after his death, a seance summons the founder of Pakistan, and he sees 'flashes of evil pictures'. Episode 1 of a ten-part documentary on Venkat Dhulipala's Creating a New Medina: the claim that Pakistan was not a vague accident but a plentifully imagined Islamic state, a new Medina, argued over in the towns of north India, and the critics who disagree.
note: Discusses the partition of India and its mass violence, and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015); reviews by F. Devji (The Wire, 2015), S. I. Khan (Marginalia Review), P. B. Mehta (Indian Express, 2015), I. Talbot (JAS, 2015); A. Jalal, The Sole Spokesman (1985).

title: The Broken Coalition
logline: In 1936 a small-town paper called the Muslim League 'neither dead nor alive'. Episode 2 goes back to the 1937 elections in the United Provinces, when Congress and the League were allies against the landlords, a Deobandi cleric campaigned for Jinnah, and nobody could yet say who was a nationalist and who a communalist.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 1; Linlithgow and Haig papers, Venkatachar memoirs and the U.P. press as quoted there; Jalal and Seal (1981).

title: Four-Anna Members
logline: Shut out of power in 1937, the Muslim League took on Nehru's campaign to win Muslims with economics. Episode 3 follows the by-elections, the war over flags, songs and schools, a Sufi scholar's telegram and a bald parrot from Rumi, as a party 'neither dead nor alive' became a mass movement.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 2; AICC Papers, the Hindustan weekly, Thanawi's collected opinions and governors' letters as quoted there.

title: Two Lawyers from Bombay
logline: In 1944 Jinnah told Gandhi to read a book on Pakistan written by Dr B. R. Ambedkar. Episode 4 follows the public argument that gave the Pakistan demand its maps, numbers and hostages, the League's answer, the failed talks on Malabar Hill, and the case against the idea that Pakistan was only a bargaining counter.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 3; Ambedkar's Thoughts on Pakistan, MRT's volumes, the Gandhi-Jinnah correspondence and Jinnah's speeches as quoted there; Jalal (1985).

title: The Ideal Goal
logline: After the Lahore Resolution, the Muslim League's leaders in the United Provinces had to explain Pakistan to Muslims who would never live in it. Episode 5 follows the pamphlets, speeches and private letters: an Islamic state, a 'laboratory', a jumping-off ground for the Muslim world, a quiet readiness to accept a smaller Pakistan, and minorities held as hostages.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 4; the pamphlets, speeches and archival letters quoted there.

title: The Other Medina
logline: Some of Pakistan's most determined Muslim opponents were men of religion. Episode 6 follows three critiques from the Deobandi camp and its allies: Sajjad's 'fraud of Islamic Pakistan', Manglori's sums for the Muslims left behind, and Seoharvi's warning that Islam would shrink into geography, plus the ulama's own plan for a united India.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 5; the Urdu tracts and articles quoted there; Metcalf (2009) on Madani.

title: Letters to Madina
logline: In 1942 a pro-Congress Urdu paper in the small town of Bijnor asked its readers what they understood by Pakistan, and printed the answers. Episode 7 follows that debate: a critic who said mass migration was impossible, a defender who promised hostages on both sides, readers from Bombay to Raichur, and letters to Jinnah asking what Pakistan would mean for those left behind.
note: Discusses the partition of India, communal politics and historical rhetoric about minorities. No graphic imagery.
source: Venkat Dhulipala, Creating a New Medina: State Power, Islam, and the Quest for Pakistan in Late Colonial North India (Cambridge University Press, 2015), chapter 6; the Madina debate and letters in the Quaid-i-Azam Papers as quoted there.

title: Eight Nights of Fire
logline: In June 2023 a police officer shot 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk in Nanterre, and France burned for eight nights. A sourced, illustrated account of the riots: the damage, the attacks on police, mayors and town halls, the phones that spread it, the second riot online, who the rioters were, and whether Gad Saad's 'suicidal empathy', especially his claim about women, holds up against the data.
note: Adult audiences: describes riot violence, arson, a death and online hate factually. Stylised imagery, no graphic content.
source: French Senate inquiry (April 2024); Interior Ministry (G. Darmanin, July 2023); Justice Ministry (E. Dupond-Moretti, Aug 2023); France Assureurs (March 2024); Ifop polls for Le Figaro (29-30 June) and Sud Radio (4-5 July 2023); EDMO and Logically fact-checks; Reuters, AFP, NPR, The Local; Cour de cassation (12 June 2026). Framing from 'Suicidal Empathy' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased and attributed, with counterpoints.

title: Who Burned France?
logline: A school strike over crowded classrooms became France's worst riots in years on 17 October 2026. A mapped, sourced account of what burned, who was arrested, what Asra Nomani's 'Chaos Inc.' investigation found, and whether the viral claim that immigrants used the student protests as cover holds up.
note: Adult audiences: describes riot violence, arson, injuries to children and police, and online hate factually. Stylised imagery, no graphic content.
source: Interior Ministry (L. Nuñez) and Justice Ministry (G. Darmanin), Oct 2026; PM S. Lecornu; Limoges prefecture; Asra Q. Nomani, Fox News Digital (9 and 20 Oct 2026); AP Fact Focus (20 Oct); NewsGuard; The Week fact check; Reuters, AP, AFP, Al Jazeera, Le Figaro, Sud Radio, actu17, Wikipedia timeline. Figures as of 23 October 2026.

title: Dying to Be Kind
logline: When Mayor Hart cranks the town's Empathy Dial to eleven, Penny Doormat has to save her spineless dad, his credit score and the whole damn town by working out when kindness helps and when it gets you robbed by a raccoon.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Dying to Be Kind (Family Cut)
logline: When Mayor Hart cranks the town's Empathy Dial to eleven, Penny Doormat has to save her too-nice dad, her fridge and her whole town by learning when kindness helps and when it backfires.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Justice-Involved Raccoon
logline: When Kindleton bans hurtful facts and renames every crime, Penny's science fair project gets cancelled for being true, and Dale gets convicted by the internet for a crime nobody can name.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Hairworm Season
logline: Kindleton assumes its brutal softball rivals secretly want participation trophies too, and Dale starts cheering for the other team so hard he jumps in the town fountain.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Blank Slate Felons
logline: Kindleton's bike thief walks free for the forty-first time, while Dale stops a robbery and gets sentenced to Masculinity Unlearning.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: The Settled Science Fair
logline: Kindleton declares all science settled, locks itself indoors over one sneeze and bans exhaling, until Penny builds a booth with a big red button that says Prove Me Wrong.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Indulgence Inc.
logline: Brightside MegaCorp starts selling Guilt Offsets, the hospital hires a surgeon for his energy, and Dale loses three organs to good vibes.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Govern Me Harder, Daddy!
logline: Mayor Hart makes everything in Kindleton free and taxes everyone at one hundred and ten percent, and Penny's lemonade stand goes bankrupt in one afternoon.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Dial M for Moderation
logline: Season finale. The Empathy Dial goes on trial for crimes against common sense, with Penny prosecuting, the Mayor defending, and Rocco as the key witness.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).

title: Too Kind to Survive?
logline: Can a society care itself to death? A calm, illustrated tour of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy': where empathy comes from, how it misfires, why it feels so good, what his critics say, and the habits worth keeping either way.
source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased, with published criticism (The Bulwark, Quillette). Also cited: Randolph Nesse on emotions, Robert Axelrod's tit-for-tat tournaments, Thomas Sowell and Rob Henderson on luxury beliefs.

title: The Things We Won’t Say
logline: Should a fact ever be hidden to spare feelings? Chapter 2 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on forbidden knowledge, softened words, compassion without conditions, and the fable of the scorpion, with the strongest counterpoints.
source: Chapter 2 ('Forbidden Knowledge') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: Fryer (2016); Harvard (2019); US DHS (2022); reporting on the 2018 Tajikistan attack.

title: Same Species, Different Rules
logline: Are all cultures equal? Chapter 3 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on the 'cultural theory of mind', harmful practices, Canada's postnational idea, England's grooming gang scandal and uneven empathy, with the strongest counterpoints.
note: Discusses child sexual exploitation, FGM and honour killings factually, without graphic detail.
source: Chapter 3 ('Cultural Theory of Mind') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: Jay Report (2014), Casey Audit (2025), UNICEF (2024), ADL (2023).

title: Second Chances
logline: Can compassion for offenders cost victims? Chapter 4 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on repeat offenders, defunding the police, the Penny case, 'sneaky' signalling and lenient courts, with the strongest counterpoints. For adults.
note: Adult audiences: discusses rape and murder factually, and one crude zoology nickname. No graphic content.
source: Chapter 4 ('Blank Slate Felons') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: BJS recidivism study (2021); Penny trial (2024); Freiburg trial (2018).

title: Settled?
logline: When does 'settled science' stop being science? Chapter 5 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on Semmelweis, falsifiability, taboo trade-offs, COVID policy, climate anxiety and youth gender medicine, with the strongest counterpoints.
source: Chapter 5 ('Settled Science, Taboo Trade-Offs') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: Cass Review (2024); New York Times (2024); Ioannidis et al. (2023); Watson et al. (2022).

title: Buying Absolution
logline: Is DEI a modern indulgence? Chapter 6 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on opportunity versus outcome, diversity statements, dropped tests, hiring in medicine and safety, and brand backlash, with the strongest counterpoints.
source: Chapter 6 ('Selling Indulgences') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: university test-policy announcements (2024); FAA litigation; AB InBev results (2023).

title: The Kindest Government
logline: Does the welfare state run on empathy? Chapter 7 of Gad Saad's 'Suicidal Empathy' on ants and socialism, New Harmony, taxation, Canada's healthcare waits, the nanny state and the military, with the strongest counterpoints. Series finale.
source: Chapter 7 ('Govern Me Harder, Daddy!') of 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), paraphrased. Public record: Fraser Institute (2023); Quebec and federal tax tables (2022).
